scope_assessment: Reviewed the complete A2/A3 diff (avatar-visualization.ts contract, avatar/visualization.ts pure mapper, 0031_avatar_visuals.sql migration, db/avatar-visuals.ts reader, release-plan.ts avatarVisualUses addition, index.ts migration registration, Number() cast, and all new tests) against the frozen R15 baseline files supplied for context (auth.ts, guest-http.ts, recommendation-http.ts, staff-runtime.ts, recommendation-service.ts, hold.ts, pricing.ts, ledger.ts, and migrations 0001-0030). Confirmed via the supplied unified diff that no route, auth, guest, staff, recommendation-service, hold, pricing, or historical migration file was touched — the change set is exactly the 9 files/1 migration described. Traced control flow by hand rather than relying on the self-reported PASS logs.

findings.title: avatar_visuals rows are not field-immutable beyond id/created_at
findings.counterexample: UPDATE avatar_visuals SET media_id=..., model_id=..., variant_id=..., ski_length_cm=... is permitted by the trigger as long as the EXACT_PROMISE re-check (avatar_visual_variant_matches) still passes for the new values; only id and created_at are protected. This differs from every other immutable-record table in the same subsystem (content_revision_records, content_outbox, content_media_objects all use a hard pricing_immutable-style block-all-mutation trigger).
findings.impact: No live actor can currently exploit this (no write route exists, and the read query's jsonb containment check against the frozen ContentRevision.avatarVisualUses grant — keyed by immutable id — silently makes a retargeted row ineligible, so retargeting fails closed at read time, confirmed by the 'digest retargeting denied' test). Risk is latent: if Phase4 or a future admin tool ever exposes a narrow 'soft-disable/reorder' write endpoint against this table without re-deriving the full immutability contract, a broader field mutation could slip through undetected.
findings.test_coverage: local-db.json test 'general model photo rights do not authorize Avatar; digest retargeting denied' demonstrates the read-time fail-closed behavior but does not assert that the table itself rejects the mutation.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: Tighten avatar_visual_guard to reject changes to layer, avatar_type, match_kind, model_id, variant_id, season, ski_length_cm, media_id, derivative_sha256, revision_id, release_id on UPDATE, permitting only state, sort_order, anchor_x/y, position_x/y and updated_at to change.
findings.required_proof: A local PostgreSQL test asserting UPDATE of any binding field on an existing row raises 23514.

findings.title: Visualization is dropped entirely (including valid ski ratios) when zero artwork exists anywhere for the member
findings.counterexample: With a SKI profile having 3 valid offered candidates and positive height/length/ratio, but metadata=[] (no visuals granted for any layer), all three candidates[direction] objects are computed with visual:null, fallback:null, yet the final gate `if(!avatar&&!boot&&!jacket&&!pants&&!DIRECTIONS.some(d=>candidates[d]?.visual))return null;` discards the entire payload including the computed skiLengthCm/skiToBodyRatio.
findings.impact: Conceptual shape in authority section 10 describes `visual: VisualRef | null` as an independent nullable field inside each candidate, implying length/ratio data should be deliverable even without artwork. The current implementation is more conservative (all-or-nothing), which is safe but under-delivers optional presentation data; no security/business-boundary consequence.
findings.test_coverage: tests/unit/avatar-visualization.test.ts 'Avatar zero visuals leaves exact business object unchanged' confirms and locks in this exact behavior; no test exercises the 'ratio without any artwork' case as a distinct scenario.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: None required for this milestone; if Phase4 needs ratio-only display before artwork exists, relax the final gate to keep per-direction candidates with visual:null instead of discarding the whole object.
findings.required_proof: Not required for PASS; note for Phase4 requirements discussion.

findings.title: Read-only avatar visual role is granted SELECT on the entire content_workspace JSON blob, not just avatar-relevant fields
findings.counterexample: GRANT SELECT ON avatar_visuals,content_workspace,content_revision_records,content_outbox,ledger_models,ledger_variants TO <role> gives the reader role visibility into the full product content-preview JSON (all draft/model marketing content, translations, media metadata for every product), not only the Avatar-purpose subset it needs.
findings.impact: Low: content_workspace holds product marketing/preview data (non-secret, non-payment, non-credential), and this milestone supplies no route that exposes this role's query results beyond the mapper output. Still broader than least-privilege.
findings.test_coverage: local-db.json 'no PUBLIC grants...' and 'read-only role...' tests confirm the role cannot mutate or read bytes/secrets, but do not test scope-minimization of the JSON read.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: Track for Phase4: consider a narrower view/materialized projection exposing only fields needed for avatar-visual eligibility instead of the full workspace blob.

validation_assessment: Self-validation evidence (197 unit tests incl. 28 Avatar, 39 real local PostgreSQL checks incl. 15 Avatar, lint/typecheck/build/secret-scan/git-diff-check) is Codex-authored and not independently re-executed here, consistent with the tools-disabled static review constraint. I independently traced the pure mapper (mapAvatarVisualization/withAvatarVisualization), the single read query in avatar-visuals.ts, and migration 0031's constraints/triggers line-by-line rather than trusting the log output, and found the claimed behaviors (fail-closed ambiguity handling, REGULAR non-guarantee, PREMIUM exact-match binding, WEAR/SNOWBOARD exclusion, rights/expiry/internal-only gating, one bounded SELECT, read-only role, business-error-before-visual-catch ordering) to be accurately implemented and consistent with the unit/DB test names supplied. Migration checksum values in migration-hashes.json/validation.json are self-reported and were not independently recomputed (no execution available), which is acceptable per task scope (local foundation only, no reruns required/claimed).
business_boundary_assessment: Confirmed by direct code inspection (not just log trust): no route/handler in the supplied R15 baseline files (recommendation-http.ts, guest-http.ts, auth.ts, staff-runtime.ts) imports or calls into packages/core/src/avatar/*, and none of those files appear in the GIT_DIFF, meaning they are byte-identical to the frozen R15 base. withAvatarVisualization invokes loadAuthorized() (the caller's authorized business loader) strictly outside its try/catch, so any HoldError/LedgerError/business exception from that loader propagates unchanged; only the internal reader.read()/mapAvatarVisualization() failure path is swallowed. The mapper performs no DB/provider/service calls, no RecommendationService.preview/select re-invocation, and never mutates its MemberRecommendation/Profile inputs (verified via structuredClone-before/after equality in tests and by inspecting that every returned object is a fresh spread/object literal).
rights_assessment: The 0031 schema and db/avatar-visuals.ts query correctly implement: (1) active-only rows via a NULLS-NOT-DISTINCT partial unique index preventing ambiguous active defaults; (2) exact PREMIUM binding enforced both by a CHECK constraint and by a re-validating BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger against the immutable ledger_variants/ledger_models identity (family, tier, catalog_season, parsed size), using fields that are themselves immutable per the existing ledger_guard; (3) purpose-specific authorization requiring an exact jsonb containment match of every identifying field (visualId keyed by the row's immutable id, layer, avatarType, match, modelId, variantId, season, skiLengthCm, mediaId, derivativeSha256) against the AvatarVisualUses array embedded in the CURRENT released, immutable ContentRevision — meaning even though non-id fields of an avatar_visuals row are technically mutable (finding AV-1), any retargeting attempt breaks this containment match and the row becomes ineligible at read time (verified by the 'digest retargeting denied' test); (4) rights validity (processed, rightsConfirmed, non-internal, rightsUntil in the future) checked in SQL and re-checked in the pure mapper; (5) no image bytes, signed/temporary URL, or credential ever leave the query or the VisualRef payload (ref() only exposes id/layer/match/derivativeSha256/revisionId/releaseId/anchor/position — no modelId/variantId/mediaId/URL). No route grants byte-serving access; this remains pure metadata eligibility as the ADR states.
